docs/development/issue-library/records/B.title: Internal import alias requirement conflicts with isolated source-copy resolution
docs/development/issue-library/records/B.symptom: The user expected internal imports to share a project alias. Tests and development tools use @/, while product engine imports remain relative and import alignment does not rewrite module specifiers.

rootCause.summary: The former repository contract forbade @/ in product sources because only the root tsconfig defined it and isolated development copies lacked equivalent resolution. The migration added the copied-skill mapping, dependency isolation, alias-aware layout enforcement and bundled resolution before changing engine imports.

docs/development/issue-library/records/B.requestedOutcome: Use configured aliases consistently for internal source imports with equivalent module resolution in development copy and release bundles, preserving package boundaries and execution order.
decisions: The 2026-10-21 user request adds alias consistency to AUTHOR1 and the Write/Refactor skill.
An alias is not an OS absolute path. Keep the existing @/* engine-root meaning during investigation.
Migrate the resolver, checker and installation contracts together before changing product imports; horizontal Align never rewrites module specifiers.
Keep the engine-external rules JSON import and the three import.meta.url runtime paths relative because they are outside the engine module alias contract.

actions.description: Record alias-aware authoring guidance and explicit migration acceptance work.

Complete the final independent READINESS1 audit that includes the migrated source state.

rootCause.summary: Source inspection confirmed same-line nested pair overwrite and incomplete gap validation. The old adapter had no preserved snapshot, so the pre-fix example was traced rather than executed.

decisions: Require exact candidate reconstruction from the original line and AST key range.

docs/development/issue-library/records/B.title: Lifecycle hook treated its own JSON receipts as source changes
docs/development/issue-library/records/B.symptom: After JSON entered the public tracked-language set, the integrated HUD test expected a lifecycle PostToolUse receipt with NO_CHANGES but observed PASS because project-local plugin data created BoxBox-owned baseline and receipt JSON inside the source snapshot.

rootCause.summary: Lifecycle snapshots used the repository-wide tracked-extension set without excluding the exact receipt namespace written by the same lifecycle hook. A project-local plugin-data directory therefore made SessionStart evidence appear as a later user JSON edit.

docs/development/issue-library/records/B.requestedOutcome: Exclude only the current project's BoxBox-owned lifecycle receipt namespace from lifecycle snapshots while continuing to inspect ordinary JSON and unrelated plugin-data JSON; restore NO_CHANGES without weakening source coverage.
decisions: Keep JSON tracked globally and leave snapshot default behavior unchanged.
Pass an explicit exact-directory exclusion only from lifecycleHook, covering all BoxBox sessions for the current project hash.
Keep the issue verifying until the final integrated check and independent audit close the current candidate.

actions.description: Add an optional explicit directory exclusion set to snapshot recursion and use it for the current project's lifecycle-owned receipt namespace.
